Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ceo
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle contains only metadata and a markdown file providing executive decision-making advice. There is no executable code, no shell commands, no network calls, and no file system operations. The SKILL.md content is purely informational and does not contain any instructions that could be interpreted as prompt injection attempts or any other malicious behavior, aligning perfectly with its stated purpose.

llm.summary: This is an instruction-only skill that provides executive leadership and prioritization guidance; its declared requirements and runtime instructions are consistent with that purpose and it does not request credentials or perform I/O.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the SKILL.md content: guidance on decision-making, prioritization, communication, people, metrics, board interactions, strategy, and self-management. Nothing requested (no env vars, binaries, or install) is out of scope for a guidance skill.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md contains only prose rules and heuristics for executive decision-making. It does not instruct the agent to run commands, read files, access environment variables, or send data to external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install specification and no code files are present. Because this is instruction-only, nothing is written to disk or downloaded during install.

dimensions.detail: No special privileges are requested: 'always' is not set and there is no install. However, 'disable-model-invocation' is also not set (default allows model-initiated invocation). That is normal for a passive guidance skill, but if you prefer to require explicit user invocation, consider enabling disable-model-invocation or controlling when the skill may be used.

llm.guidance: This skill is instruction-only and appears coherent with its stated goal of offering CEO-style guidance. It does not request credentials or perform I/O, so it poses low technical risk. Consider: (1) provenance — the skill has no homepage or author information, so verify the advice aligns with your organization’s policies; (2) accuracy and bias — treat the rules as heuristics, not legal/financial advice; and (3) invocation controls — enable disable-model-invocation or require explicit user consent if you want to prevent autonomous use by the agent.
